draft_findings.finding: Product-level rebuild from J&J's own disclosed lines puts Q3 sales at ~$25.4-25.6bn, a beat of ~0-1% on the $25.38bn mean, below the 1-3.9% habitual beat: Q3-25 comps carry one-offs (Simponi $687m, Remicade $476m, EP +9.7%, Abiomed +15.6%) and FX swings from +1.0pt in Q2 to about -0.2pt.

FY26 consensus (revenue $101.38bn, EPS $11.085) already sits at the top of / above the midpoint of guidance, while the euro has fallen to 1.116 (Oct 12) from the 1.15 the July guide assumed; the Q4 FX update trims ~$0.15-0.2bn of reported sales and ~$0.02-0.03 EPS, so the reported raise lands at or slightly below the street even with an operational raise.

J&J IR's 2026-09-16 phasing note says the ~$0.64 Firefly+Sail dilution primarily relates to Q3 transactions while the $2.53 mean spans $2.31-2.81, so the headline adjusted EPS risks printing at/below the mean on a mechanical IPR&D basis.

MedTech chief (2026-09-09) declined to confirm H2 acceleration, citing tougher Q3/Q4 comps, lingering EP competitive intensity, Middle East disruption and China EP VBP later this year; Impella Class I recall (FDA 2026-07-02).

premortem_draft: If JNJ rallies hard, the likeliest cause is Q1/Q2: an Innovative Medicine beat (Tremfya +71% in Q2, ICOTYDE 17,000 patients with all big-3 PBMs, Wolk 'where the analysts are, we should see a number more') large enough that the raise clears the street even after FX, plus confident 2027 language ahead of the Dec 8 review. Evidence already in hand: five straight sales beats of 1.0-3.86%; Q2 IM +27% q/q in Tremfya. Sized within Q1's +0.8 upper range.
